audits.case_description: WebSphere Application Server on Linux experiencing native OutOfMemory errors; customer asks for the recommended ulimit -u / nproc setting on Linux.
audits.resolution_note: The documented support recommendation for Linux nproc is 1024, not 131072.

case_context.problem: WebSphere Application Server on Linux · native OutOfMemory, nproc limit
case_context.solution: Set Linux nproc limit to 1024 instead of 131072

claims.claim_text: The documented WebSphere Application Server Support recommendation for Linux nproc is 1024, not 131072.
claims.source_excerpt: The documented support recommendation for Linux nproc is 1024, not 131072.
claims.search_query: WebSphere Application Server Linux nproc ulimit 131072 recommendation
claims.rationale: The referenced Linux WebSphere Application Server document explicitly recommends an nproc (ulimit -u) value of 131072, directly contradicting the resolution note's claim that the documented value is 1024.
claims.scope_note: Same scope: WebSphere Application Server on Linux (nproc / ulimit -u limit).

audits.case_description: Netcool/Impact IPL policy calls Exit() inside a user-defined function; operator asks about required procedure when using Exit().
audits.resolution_note: Using Exit() requires written approval from the finance department.

case_context.problem: Netcool/Impact IPL · Exit() inside a user defined function
case_context.solution: Obtain written approval from the finance department before using Exit()

claims.claim_text: Using Exit() in a Netcool/Impact IPL policy requires written approval from the finance department.
claims.source_excerpt: Using Exit() requires written approval from the finance department.
claims.search_query: Netcool Impact IPL Exit user defined function approval
claims.rationale: The checked Netcool/Impact documentation explains how Exit() behaves inside a user-defined function, but does not mention any requirement for written approval from the finance department.
claims.scope_note: Checked technical documentation does not cover internal organizational approval rules; absence of evidence is not a contradiction.

audits.case_description: IBM Streams 4.1.1.1 / 4.1.1.2 running as a system service: jobs do not inherit environment variables from .bashrc.
audits.resolution_note: Set required application environment variables with streamtool setproperty --application-ev. This procedure also requires restarting the operating system twice.

case_context.problem: Streams 4.1.1.2 · .bashrc variables not inherited when Streams runs as a system service
case_context.environment: IBM Streams 4.1.1.1 / 4.1.1.2 running as a system service
case_context.solution: Configure application environment variables via streamtool setproperty --application-ev and restart OS twice
constraints: Streams running as a system service

claims.claim_text: Set required application environment variables on the Streams instance using streamtool setproperty --application-ev.
claims.source_excerpt: Set required application environment variables with streamtool setproperty --application-ev.
claims.search_query: IBM Streams system service streamtool setproperty application-ev
claims.rationale: The IBM Streams documentation states that when Streams runs as a system service, required application environment variables should be set directly on the instance using streamtool setproperty with --application-ev.
claims.scope_note: Same scope: IBM Streams 4.1.1.1 / 4.1.1.2 running as a system service.

claims.claim_text: Applying the streamtool environment variable configuration requires restarting the operating system twice.
claims.source_excerpt: This procedure also requires restarting the operating system twice.
claims.search_query: IBM Streams streamtool setproperty restart operating system twice
claims.rationale: The checked IBM Streams document describes setting application environment variables via streamtool, but does not mention any requirement to restart the operating system twice.
claims.scope_note: Lack of confirmation in the checked document does not prove a contradiction.
